opener_episode.title: Bitcoin & Sports Teams Are The Best Hedge Against Inflation
opener_episode.why: The only recent episode about scarce trophy assets as stores of value, which is the natural bridge to blue-chip art as an alternative asset for the wealthy. Everything else is AI/macro/Bitcoin, which Avery can't speak to credibly. Note: the guest's identity (which Chris Kelly) is unverified; confirm before using the name.

angles.headline: Trophy assets: what the ultra-wealthy buy besides Bitcoin and sports teams
angles.pitch: Avery advises celebrities, athletes and high-net-worth clients on buying and investing in art, and can explain how blue-chip art behaves as a scarce asset (e.g., placing a $100K+ Hap Tivey work with Kris Jenner at Art Basel Miami Beach 2024).
angles.builds_on: Chris Kelly episode (Sept 23) on scarce assets as inflation hedges

angles.headline: Selling blue-chip art online before collectors trusted the internet
angles.pitch: Avery launched ArtLife.com in 2015 as one of the first online-only blue-chip galleries and scaled it to eight figures a year with his 'Click & Mortar' model, a founder story about digital distribution of a trust-heavy asset.
angles.builds_on: Pomp's founder/operator interviews (e.g., Christopher Zook, Sept 28) and his audience-first media playbook

angles.headline: Art meets crypto: what the NFT era actually taught an art dealer
angles.pitch: Avery's ArtGrails sold Michael Cohen's prison badge as an NFT (Vanity Fair, 2021) and launched with an Ozuna art drop (Rolling Stone), giving him first-hand lessons on digital ownership and collector behavior.
angles.builds_on: The show's core Bitcoin/digital-asset audience (Jordi Visser, Sept 19 & 26)

booking.route: No published guest form or booking email found. Best documented routes: Pomp's X account (@APompliano) and anthonypompliano.com; a third-party directory (ContactOut/Listen Notes) lists Tyler Lambers as producer/editor (reach via LinkedIn).
booking.contact: @APompliano (X); Tyler Lambers, producer/editor per third-party directory (unverified)

format: Near-daily cadence; video on YouTube (~530K-650K subs, third-party) plus audio. Mix of remote and in-person interviews (unverified per episode). Typical guests: macro investors, fund managers, Bitcoin/AI executives, founders. Episodes are usually under an hour (unverified). Pompliano's Miami base is unconfirmed.
red_flags: Content is overwhelmingly Bitcoin/AI/macro; no art-market or collectibles guest found, so the pitch must be framed as alternative assets / founder story. Very guest-selective, high-profile show. No verified booking route.
